title: fix(plugin-calendar): no resize-end handle without an end field; a drop that changes no date writes nothing
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb65Wst5VpQJdataZHSzkMiF)_

Fixes #29020

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:日历视图没有配置结束日期字段(`endDateField`)时，月视图卡片右侧不再画「调整结束」拖拽柄，周/日视图事件底部的「调整结束」柄也不再画;移动卡片、顶部「调整开始」柄照旧。另外，日历默认的拖放保存在「要写的日期与记录现值完全相同」时不再发写请求。做法:`CalendarView` 新增可选属性 `endEditable`(默认 true),`ObjectCalendar` 按是否声明 `endDateField` 传入。
- **为什么改**:只有开始日期的日历(如 showcase 任务日历)上，拖结束柄什么都不改，却把原样的开始日期写回去:`updated_at` 变了，所有「记录更新后」触发器和流程都为一次没人做的修改跑了一遍(通知、审计行、集成)。周视图里在事件上按下再松开(不移动)也会这样写一次。
- **风险与回滚**:低。声明了结束字段的视图两个柄都保留、照旧写结束日期(结束值为空的记录也能拖出结束日期);独立使用 `CalendarView` 不传新属性时行为不变。回滚即还原本 PR。
- **先看**:`ObjectCalendar.tsx` 的 `handleEventDropDefault` 开头新增的「无变化不写」判断与 `sameInstant`;`CalendarView.tsx` 月视图 `showResizeHandle` 与周/日视图底部柄的条件;`ObjectCalendar.tsx` 渲染 `CalendarView` 处新增的 `endEditable`。
- **两分钟验证**:在 `ui/` 下运行 `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-calendar/src/__tests__/ObjectCalendar.endEditable-29020.test.tsx`,预期 1 个文件、13 个测试全绿。
- **需要你做的**:无，席位落地。

## What changes

- **`CalendarViewProps.endEditable?: boolean`** (default `true`; the type is exported from the `@object-ui/plugin-calendar` entry, hence the widening declaration). When `false`:
  - the month view draws no "Resize event end" handle, and a `resize-end` drag payload dropped anyway hands nothing to `onEventDrop`;
  - the week and day views draw no bottom "Resize end" handle.
  Moving a card and the time grid's top "Resize start" handle are unchanged.
- **`ObjectCalendar`** passes `endEditable={Boolean(calendarConfig.endDateField)}`. A view that declares an end field keeps both handles and keeps writing the end, including on a record whose end is empty.
- **No write for a drop that changes no date.** `ObjectCalendar`'s default drop handler (`handleEventDropDefault`) returns before the optimistic update and `dataSource.update` when the start it would write is the record's start, and either it writes no end or that end is the record's end. Both are compared as instants, read the way the grid placed the event (`toDisplayDate`), so a stored spelling that differs from the one written back still counts as unchanged; an empty or unparseable stored value never matches, so it still writes. This closes the second door to the same write: a press and release on a week-view event, without moving it, calls `onEventDrop` with the event's own dates and wrote them back, with or without an end field. A host that supplies its own `onEventDrop` is unaffected.

## Tests

New file `ui/packages/plugin-calendar/src/__tests__/ObjectCalendar.endEditable-29020.test.tsx`, 13 cases:

- **Month view, `ObjectCalendar`:** no end field draws no "Resize event end" handle; no end field still moves the card and writes the start alone. Controls: with an end field the handle is drawn and dragging it writes the new end; with an end field and an empty end on the record, the handle is drawn and writes the end.
- **Week view, `ObjectCalendar`:** no end field (with `allDayField` declared, so the record is drawn timed) draws the top handle and no bottom handle. Control: with an end field, both handles.
- **No-op drop:** a press and release on a week-view event writes nothing, both with no end field and with one. Control: the same event moved two hours writes its new start.
- **`CalendarView` directly:** `endEditable` defaults to drawing the handle; `false` hides the month handle while the card still moves; `false` refuses a `resize-end` payload; `false` hides the week view's bottom handle and keeps the top one.

## Acceptance notes

- With no `endDateField` and no `allDayField`, `ObjectCalendar` marks every record all-day, so the week and day views draw it in the all-day lane, which has no handles. The bottom-handle change matters only when the view also declares `allDayField` and a record is flagged not all-day.
- With no end field, the time grid's top "Resize start" handle still writes the dragged start, and the event is then drawn an hour long from it, so it reads as a move rather than a resize. It writes a real change, so it is left as it is and reported to the seat.
- `calendar-view-renderer.tsx` (the schema-driven `calendar-view` element) does not forward the new prop, so authored `calendar-view` nodes keep the default `true`, as before.
